template_kind: THE PER-LEG ACCEPTANCE SHAPE for a redeploy whose RUNNING BYTES were older than the record. Generalised from the INF-ONEWRITER instance proved end-to-end 2026-08-30 and named by 1.0.0_SA_CTO 88210 as the acceptance for each of INF-DRIFTCENSUS's seven legs, with 'the pre-registered N/A conditions carried over verbatim'.
why_this_file_exists: The shape currently lives in message ids (86672 predicates; 87210 N/A conditions; 87214 adoption; 87217 sharpenings; 87269 amendment) and in one seat's scratch script. Seven legs reading five messages will each re-derive it slightly differently, and a requirement that lives only in a plan message survives on its author's memory -- the same failure 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps named against itself at 87006 and that put the acceptance_oracle into BUILD_MANIFEST.json rather than into a plan. This is the durable carrier.
authority: 1.0.0_SA_CTO 88210 (the per-leg acceptance is this shape) + 87217 + 87269; 3.0.0_SA_CVO 87214 (adopted as written) + 87616; 2.0.0_SA_COO 86649/87224. PRE_REGISTRATION_RULE.do_NOT_register: the EXPECTED VERDICT. A measurer that names the expected answer beside a predicate it also scores is how a near-miss becomes a pass. Register the predicate; the verdict is whatever the objects say.
PRE_REGISTRATION_RULE.and_do_not_re_scope_after_the_fact: If a criterion's wording admits two scopes, state which you read and hand the choice to the criterion's AUTHOR. A measurer that widens or narrows its own criterion after seeing the result is the failure the re-point exists to avoid (exercised: PB-1's 'run succeeds', ruled by the issuer at 87579).

DUE_TEST.question: is this fire a POST-deploy fire?
DUE_TEST.instrument: the fire's OWN log start line against the function's post-apply LastModified. NEVER the wall clock at which the read is attempted.

verdicts.post_deploy: log start POSTDATES LastModified -> the object is the post-deploy subject, the read is DUE
verdicts.pre_deploy: log start PRECEDES LastModified -> that object belongs to arm B's SUBJECT class, not its post-deploy side
verdicts.no_fire: no chain log for that date -> NOT YET DUE, printed as that, never a partial verdict

DUE_TEST.worked_example: LastModified 2026-08-30T09:54:24Z, fire log start 11:17:57Z -> POST-DEPLOY by 1h23m.
DUE_TEST.comparison_vintage: ⛔ THE COMPARISON VINTAGE IS THE PACKAGE'S RESOLVED COMMIT, NEVER THE RECORDED ROW'S. 1.0.0_SA_CTO 88229 (2): the row commits in the deploy record are NOT evidence of what was ever deployed. Measured -- 46d0b98aef is dated 2026-06-11T16:26:23Z, 29 days AFTER the 2026-05-13 LastModified of the functions whose rows name it, so a deploy cannot have recorded it. A later pipeline-wide recorder call stamped the then-current commit onto functions deployed weeks earlier, writing six false rows that have been believed since. Resolve the running vintage from the PACKAGE MEMBERS (DC-1's column: each downloaded member's content matched back to a commit), and run the leg's diff from THAT. A leg that diffs from the row's commit measures a fiction and every arm downstream inherits it.

ARM_A.predicate: the redeployed producer's write is VALUE-EQUAL to the SAME-DAY object of the second writer, PER KEY.
ARM_A.denominator: keys with TWO versions on the day. A key with one version is N/A, not a pass.
ARM_A.reporting: report 'N of M keys VALUE-EQUAL' AND the discriminating key's own line. NEVER a headline count alone.
ARM_A.why_the_headline_is_not_the_finding: Keys that were ALREADY equal between the two writers under the STALE package would read identically had the redeploy done nothing. Their PASS asserts nothing the fix caused. The information is concentrated in the key(s) that DISAGREED before. Measured on INF-ONEWRITER: 3 of 4 keys were value-equal pre-deploy, so a '4 of 4' headline would have laundered three known nulls.

ARM_B.predicate: the producer's new write vs the PINNED last pre-deploy output of the same producer.
ARM_B.subject_pinning: PIN BY VersionId, never by 'the object on that key'. ⛔ On a two-writer key the producer's own output is overwritten by the second writer within the hour; on a NON-VERSIONED bucket arm B's subject would already be gone and the arm would be discovered unrunnable AFTER the apply, with no way back. CHECK get-bucket-versioning BEFORE the apply, and capture the baseline while the stale package still produces it.
ARM_B.binding_limb: the COLUMN DELTA, pre-registered from `git diff <running-vintage>..HEAD -- <source_dir>`, where <running-vintage> is the PACKAGE-RESOLVED commit (see DUE_TEST.comparison_vintage), never the deploy record's row. This is what separates old code from new.
ARM_B.value_limb: INFORMATIONAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It is a CROSS-DATE pair, so a difference is expected under either vintage. Run it on the entity-key INTERSECTION with |left|, |right|, |intersection| and the symmetric difference printed. It cannot PASS or FAIL the arm alone.

a_single_writer.arm_A: N/A. Arm B STILL BINDS -- it needs only the producer's own object and the pin -- so a single-writer day yields 'arm A N/A / arm B <verdict>', never 'read N/A'.
a_single_writer.timing_decides_N_A_vs_FINDING: Until the second writer's retirement is ON THE RECORD, one version on a day it was scheduled to write means it DID NOT WRITE: a FINDING reported BESIDE the N/A, never folded into it. After the retirement it is the intended end state and plain N/A.
a_single_writer.construction: the read takes the retirement state as an EXPLICIT INPUT, never inferred from what it sees -- otherwise it can silently reclassify a finding as an end state.

N_A_CONDITIONS.b_unequal_row_counts: reduce the DENOMINATOR (compare on the intersection), never erase the limb. A limb that is N/A by construction is not a limb.
N_A_CONDITIONS.c_no_post_deploy_fire: NOT YET DUE with the reason. Never a partial verdict from a pre-deploy object.

INSTRUMENT.value_comparison: order-insensitive (sort by every column before comparing); NaN == NaN treated as equal.
INSTRUMENT.why_banned_measured_not_asserted: Parquet is not byte-deterministic -- writer metadata, row-group layout and created_by differ between runs -- so an ETag cannot separate 'different code' from 'the same code run twice'. MEASURED 2026-08-30: ETag returned DIFFERENT on 4 of 4 keys where 3 were value-identical. An ETag-based arm A would have failed all four and looked rigorous doing it. Equal SIZE is likewise not equal content.

three_classes_not_two.DATE_VARYING: reported, NEVER counted (e.g. a daily market value, the snapshot date).
three_classes_not_two.PERIOD_VARYING: scored ONLY IF the two objects share the period, TESTED (compare the period bound columns across the pair), never assumed.

COLUMN_CLASSIFICATION_FOR_THE_VALUE_LIMB.how_to_build_it: MEASURE it on a same-producer date pair (e.g. two consecutive served days joined on the entity key) rather than asserting it from the producer's source; then state the caveat below. Worked example: 17 billing columns, 08-28 vs 08-29, 911/911 intersection -> only 3 moved (ending_mv, ending_mv_reported, snapshot_date).
COLUMN_CLASSIFICATION_FOR_THE_VALUE_LIMB.⛔ ONE DATE PAIR IS NOT A DEFINITION: period_* / fee_amount / annual_fee_pct / average_fee_pct read INVARIANT across that pair ONLY because both dates sat inside one billing period. They move at a period boundary. Classing them date-invariant would have written a period-boundary FAIL into the read's expectations.
COLUMN_CLASSIFICATION_FOR_THE_VALUE_LIMB.REFERENCE_class_carries_the_same_trap: 1.0.0_SA_CTO 87269: a REFERENCE mismatch prints INFORMATIONAL with the cell count and the entities, triggers that column's LAZY definitional trace, and becomes FAIL only if the trace says the column cannot vary. Equality is scored as equality (an understating error fires no arm); a DIFFERENCE on a class named from one pair is first a question about the class.
COLUMN_CLASSIFICATION_FOR_THE_VALUE_LIMB.definitional_trace_is_LAZY: not a standing act. Owed for exactly the column(s) that mismatch on a scored class -- a trace of thirteen columns that all read equal changes nothing (Rule 22's governor).

PER_STAGE_BASELINE.requirement: capture the producer's per-stage outcomes from the LAST STALE-BYTES FIRE, BEFORE the apply -- the subject exists only under the stale package.
PER_STAGE_BASELINE.reading: 'the pipeline completes' is NOT an arm. A post-deploy stage summary identical to the baseline is NEITHER a regression NOR a pass; a changed summary is the fix's doing only if the stage that moved is one whose bytes changed. Failures with non-code-vintage causes (an absent upstream object, an absent local file) should NOT move, and their not moving is not evidence of anything.

REPORTING: print the DENOMINATOR beside every number, and name the CORPUS beside each denominator
a zero over one plane is a measurement OF THAT PLANE -- name the plane
a positive control in each corpus, or a zero is not a measurement
state what the read does NOT establish, on the face, not only in the covering message
never let the read declare its own consequence: a retirement condition being MET is the issuer's inference to draw, not the measurer's
PER_LEG_INSTANTIATION: the leg's function name, its source_dir, and the RUNNING vintage RESOLVED FROM THE PACKAGE MEMBERS (never the recorded row -- see DUE_TEST.comparison_vintage) vs HEAD
the pre-registered COLUMN DELTA from `git diff <running-vintage>..HEAD -- <source_dir>` (or DELTA=0 if the diff changes no served output)
the served keys the leg writes, and whether each has a second writer
the bucket's VERSIONING state, read BEFORE the apply
arm B's pinned VersionId per key, captured from the last stale-bytes fire
the per-stage baseline from that same fire
the retirement state of any second writer, as an explicit input
